label: a2 commitment: GO choosing a2 after no reward, and D2 after a2 -> S2 (mid-episode)
explanation: Reset-gate unit that fires only when the agent is (about to be) choosing a2. It never fires at D1 or on any a1 trial (10 of 58k activations). 78% of the activation mass is at GO when the agent picks a2 (its own upcoming choice, a legitimate computation; choice logit < -4.4 in all of them), and it is strongest when the previous trial went unrewarded (in_rew = 0). It fires much more weakly when the previous trial was rewarded. The other 22% is at D2 after a2 led to S2 (common): small activations, about 0.1-0.2 of max, and they continue through runs of rewarded a2->S2 trials. It does not fire at D2 when the transition is rare (S1 shown) or when reward input is 1. Firing is also gated by a slow, episode-level factor: rate peaks at episode trials 20-59, is low before trial 10, and is zero after trial 80. Restricting to ep_trial 10-69 raises dev F1 from 0.40 to 0.54 (mass recall 0.95). Within the a2 context it also prefers episodes that started with S2 good and high value. Precision stays around 0.39, because many GO-a2-unrewarded steps in the same episode range stay silent. That suggests a slowly drifting hidden-state component that I could not capture. No future variable is used (action at GO is the agents own choice).
